modules.title: 一次退款申请中，顾客动作和系统回应怎样连接
用户用例怎样描述系统行为

items.title: 围绕一个参与者目标
items.text: 先明确谁要完成什么，以及什么事件触发这次交互，避免把多个无关功能塞进一个用例。

items.title: 交替写动作和回应
items.text: 每一步都说明参与者做什么、系统显示或改变什么，让外部行为可以被讨论和检查。

items.title: 补上重要例外
items.text: 超期、资料不完整或重复提交等条件会改变结果，需要写清系统怎样结束或帮助用户恢复。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: {c:user-story} 简短说明用户、目标和原因；{c:use-case} 展开参与者与系统的交互；{c:user-flow} 用路径图呈现页面和决策分支；{c:test-case} 再用具体输入和步骤检查其中一条规则。

lessonPractice.title: 下面哪组内容最适合作为“顾客申请退款”的用户用例？

options.label: 顾客在可退款订单中提交原因；系统检查期限并显示退款结果；超期或重复申请时说明原因和下一步
options.feedback: 对。它围绕一个参与者目标，写出了触发条件、顾客动作、系统回应、成功结果和重要例外。

options.label: 作为顾客，我希望申请退款，以便取回不需要商品的费用
options.feedback: 这是用户故事，说明了用户、目标和原因，但没有展开系统交互、条件与例外。

options.label: RefundController 调用 PaymentService，再把状态写入 refunds 表
options.feedback: 这是内部实现。用例应描述顾客与系统之间可观察的行为，不要求预先决定控制器、服务和数据表。

en.title: Which option works best as the use case for “a customer requests a refund”?

options.label: The customer submits a reason for an eligible order; the system checks the deadline and shows the result; expired or duplicate requests explain why and what to do next
options.feedback: Correct. It centers on one actor goal and includes the trigger, interaction, system response, successful result, and important exceptions.

options.label: As a customer, I want to request a refund so I can recover the cost of an unwanted item
options.feedback: That is a user story. It states the user, goal, and reason without describing the interaction and exceptions.

options.label: RefundController calls PaymentService and writes the status to the refunds table
options.feedback: That is internal implementation. A use case describes observable behavior without choosing controllers, services, or tables.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请根据我提供的退款规则整理“顾客申请退款”用户用例，写清参与者、触发条件、前置条件、顾客动作、系统回应、成功结果和重要例外。规则缺失时先列问题，不要自行决定退款期限，也不要展开控制器、接口或数据库实现。整理后检查每个结束状态是否都能被顾客看见并理解。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Using only the refund rules I provide, write the “customer requests a refund” use case with its actor, trigger, preconditions, customer actions, system responses, successful result, and important exceptions. List missing rules as questions instead of inventing a refund window, and do not expand into controllers, APIs, or database design. Then check that every ending is visible and understandable to the customer.

learning.assumes: You can describe a feature goal but may omit system responses and failure outcomes.
learning.outcome: You can define the actor, trigger, main interaction, exceptions, and observable results for one goal, then distinguish a use case from a user story, user flow, and test case.

modules.title: Connect customer actions and system responses in one refund request
How a use case describes system behavior

items.title: Center on one actor goal
items.text: Name who is trying to achieve what and what triggers the interaction.

items.title: Alternate actions and responses
items.text: State what the actor does and what the system displays or changes at every step.

items.title: Include important exceptions
items.text: Explain how expired, incomplete, or duplicate requests end or return to a recoverable state.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: A {c:user-story} states the user, goal, and reason. A {c:use-case} expands the interaction, a {c:user-flow} diagrams paths, and a {c:test-case} checks one rule with specific inputs.
